title: Fact Check: Did Trump post an image of himself with a ghostly figure of Abraham Lincoln?
excerpt: Trump had earlier compared himself to George Washington and Abraham Lincoln
content:
WASHINGTON, DC: A picture circulating on social media claims to show a post by President Donald Trump, showing a photo of himself with ghostly figures of Abraham Lincoln and a colonial-era man, and calling himself the best president in United States history. The claim has sparked speculation about its authenticity and called for a fact-check.

Claim: Trump posted an image of himself with ghostly Abraham Lincoln

The rumor surfaced as a screenshot, claiming to show a post by Trump on his official Truth Social handle.

The alleged post shows an image of Trump, along with ghostly figures of Lincoln and a colonial-era man.

The image was accompanied by an overlay text stating, “BEST PRESIDENT IN THE HISTORY OF AMERICA.”

The post has garnered tens of thousands of views as of this writing, garnering mixed reactions from online users.

While many believe it is an authentic post by the president, others dismiss it as fake.

Fact Check: Donald Trump made no such post

Although Trump posted an image of himself on Truth Social along with the same caption, the original post does not include any image of a ghostly Lincoln and a colonial-era man.

The original image was posted by a handle called ‘Republican Party News,’ which was reported by Trump.

A look at Trump Truth Social and other commentary accounts on X, which automatically archives all his social media posts, found no post that has ghostly figures.

Additional searches on his other social media handles, such as Facebook and X, also found no such post.

A search on Google to check if he had posted and then deleted returned no results, which, if true, would have been widely covered by credible news outlets.

Trump once compared himself to George Washington and Abraham Lincoln

Although the post is fake, Trump had earlier compared himself to George Washington and Abraham Lincoln.

During a speech at the White House Rose Garden last year, Trump claimed that Washington and Lincoln never “put out eight wars,” adding that he had done so during his presidency.

“It’s going to be very tough to beat Washington and Lincoln, but we’re going to give it a try. Right? Hey, they didn’t put out eight wars. Nine coming. All right. We put out eight wars, and the ninth is coming, believe it or not,” Trump said.

He said that he felt “angry” when a reporter once called him the “third best president,” behind Washington and Lincoln.
